newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on mild weekend weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on mild weekend weather.

text.p: The absence of a crop-damaging frost over the weekend and commercial selling pressured CBOT corn futures to a lower close, traders said.
"We came in and there wasn't any frost talk over the weekend and that pressured it a little," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
But losses were limited by potential frost early this week and again late this week in the northern portion of the U.S. corn growing region, they said.
Meteorologists early Monday said two cold weather systems were forecast for the U.S. Midwest this week.

Corn futures were underpinned by bullish input from Friday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook which called for below to much below normal temperatures in the Midwest from September 26 through September 30.

Also Friday's USDA Cattle on Feed report, which showed August placements at 19 percent above a year ago, underpinned prices. The placement tally was above average expectations for a 12.1 percent increase in placements. The hike in the number of cattle on feed will boost corn consumption, traders said.
Corn closed one to three cents per bushel lower, with December down one at $3.13-1/4.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 43,000 contracts, down from 51,600 Friday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options Smith Barney bought 3,000 May $3.60 calls at 8-3/4 cents.
Corn options volume was estimated at 15,000 contracts, down from 18,468 Friday.
